principles.text: Angry, detailed customer emails are a PMF signal. When projects stall at the same revenue, double down on the one people care about.
Build only from what paying customers ask for. If three paying customers ask for the same thing, it might be worth it.
Start with free credits instead of a paywall, and launch pricing tiers from day one.
First half of a customer call, shut up and listen while they walk through their workflow; then pitch what they didn't know they needed.
Bootstrap if you can. Raising money is not an accomplishment, just a necessary part of the process when you want to accelerate.

sampleQA.question: How do I know which of my projects has product-market fit?

answer.text: Watch for customers who write long, angry emails or complain instead of leaving. Ask why they cared enough to write; there's probably something there.
If several projects stall at the same revenue level, kill the rest and double down on that one. You can't work on a bunch of things at once.
Strong signals: someone at a large company paying with a personal card to skip procurement, or customers manually resubscribing after their card failed.

sampleQA.question: How should I price a developer API at launch?

answer.text: Give a set amount of free credits rather than paywalling; when credits run out, users subscribe. Churn is lower and you get feedback from people who tried it.
Have tiers from the start. At Stock Alarm, adding tiers roughly doubled MRR almost instantly.
Test a cheaper tier. A $25/mo developer tier tripled signups and conversions in his PostHog experiments.
If free-tier fraud spikes, gate by email: verified work emails get 1,000 credits a month, free emails get 250 once.

sampleQA.question: How do I get my first 10K users with no budget?

answer.text: Treat 0-10K users as a separate process from 10K-100K+. On Quora, answer questions that already have thousands of views and disclose your affiliation.
Post where your buyers already hang out, like Reddit and Quora, and optimize App Store keywords.
Build a programmatic SEO page per entity. Stock Alarm made one for each of its 12-13K tickers, linking back to the marketing site.
Use Ahrefs MCP with Claude Code to find low-difficulty, high-volume keywords per service, then write posts for them.
